key_insight: A correct answer does not guarantee a useful reasoning trace. ReDiST proposes tailoring intermediate reasoning to the target student so that supervision is both informative and accessible.
problem_solved: Reasoning traces can fail to improve learning beyond answer-only supervision when their content or difficulty does not suit the student model.
method: Start from the student model’s own reasoning attempts.
Revise answer-correct drafts with attention to intermediate content and accessibility to the target learner.
Use the constructed traces for student-conditioned reasoning distillation in evidence-rich tasks.
impact: This approach could help practitioners design reasoning supervision around what a student model can learn, rather than answer correctness alone. The supplied abstract is truncated and provides no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline: student attempt → trace revision → reasoning distillation.
Side-by-side example: correct but hard-to-follow trace versus student-accessible trace.
Two-axis diagram: intermediate-content quality and student accessibility.
Teacher–student icons with evidence documents to illustrate evidence-rich reasoning.
paper_title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
paper_authors: Shaoang Li, Yanhang Shi, Yufei Li, Mingfu Liang, Frank Shyu
